title: How Much Fiber in Almonds? 3.5g per Ounce
description: Almonds: about 3.5 g of fiber per 1 oz (13% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in almonds?
intro: Almonds rank #1 of 7 nuts, seeds, and treats on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in almonds by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in almonds?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists nuts, almonds at 12.5 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 oz (about 23 almonds); 28.4 g) therefore has about 3.5 g of fiber and 164 calories. That is 13% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 14% of a 25 g day and 9% of a 38 g day.
Almonds have more fiber per ounce than most common nuts. A standard one-ounce handful gives about 3.5 g, though it also carries around 160 calories.

sections.heading: Whole almonds, almond butter, almond milk
paragraphs: Almond butter keeps the fiber of the almonds it is made from, so 2 tablespoons is in a similar range to a one-ounce handful. Check the label.
Almond milk is mostly water and has almost no fiber. Almond flour keeps fiber but is used in small amounts per serving of baked goods.

sections.heading: How almonds compare with other nuts, seeds, and treats
paragraphs: Of the 7 nuts, seeds, and treats on this site, almonds rank #1 for fiber per typical serving and #2 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 2.2 g of fiber per 100 calories, in the middle of the range for the foods on this site.

Close neighbors by serving: [dark chocolate](/fiber-in-dark-chocolate) at 3.1 g (1 oz (70–85% cacao)); [pistachios](/fiber-in-pistachios) at 2.9 g (1 oz (about 49 kernels)); [flaxseed](/fiber-in-flaxseed) at 2.8 g (1 tbsp, whole). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), almonds are #44 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding almonds to your day
paragraphs: Pre-portion one-ounce snack bags, or add a tablespoon of sliced almonds to oatmeal or salads.

Example: 1 oz almonds, 1 apple. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 7.9 g of fiber, with 3.5 g from the almonds. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of almonds?
faqs.a: 12.5 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Nuts, almonds). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in almonds (1/4 cup)?
faqs.a: About 4.5 g, for 35.8 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Which nut has the most fiber?
faqs.a: Among common nuts on this site, almonds lead per ounce at about 3.5 g (1 oz (about 23 almonds)). Pistachios are close at about 2.9 g (1 oz (about 49 kernels)).
Very little. Most of the almond solids are strained out.
